subject: A Pokemon deal finder for your price-checker roundup
subjectAlt: One tool category missing from your Pokemon price-check post
body:
I run PokemonDealFinder (pokemondealfinder.com), a free tool that compares live eBay Pokemon card listings against recent market references and surfaces the ones that appear to be priced below market.

Your post on the best websites for checking Pokemon card prices covers the valuation and scanner side well - PriceCharting, TCGplayer, PokeScreener and the rest. The step it doesn't cover is finding listings that are currently under market in the first place.

If you ever expand the piece to include tools for that, it might be useful to readers. No worries either way.

body:
I run PokemonDealFinder (pokemondealfinder.com). Your Trading Card Statistics (2026) roundup covers the grading boom and record auctions thoroughly, but there's no figure in it for how ungraded Pokemon card values are actually distributed.

We track a catalogue of priced English Pokemon cards and analysed it. As of the {{snapshotDate}} snapshot: of the {{population}} priced, English, non-specialty cards we hold a raw market reference for, {{under5Pct}}% are under $5 raw, {{under25Pct}}% are under $25, and only {{over100Pct}}% are $100 or more. Median raw reference: ${{median}} USD.

Methodology and a dated chart: pokemondealfinder.com/market-data/pokemon-card-value-distribution - there to cite if you add a line on ungraded value spread.

body:
Enjoyed this - the No Bids + Pokecardvalues + Gixen combo is close to how I do it too.

The one manual step in that flow is checking whether a listing is actually below what the card sells for. I run PokemonDealFinder (pokemondealfinder.com), which does that part automatically: it scans live eBay listings across a few marketplaces, matches each to a specific card, and flags the ones priced under recent sold value. Free, no signup.

Might be worth a mention if you ever revisit the piece. It also has a page on how Pokemon card values actually break down - most tracked cards are only worth a few dollars raw - at pokemondealfinder.com/market-data/pokemon-card-value-distribution.

Re: your "30 Years of Pokemon TCG in Data" guide - the era-by-era median card values and set-completion costs are a great cut of the data.

I run PokemonDealFinder and recently ran a related one: the distribution of raw market references across the ~21,800 priced English non-specialty cards we track (210 sets, 1,025 species - same species count you landed on). ~65% have a raw reference under $5; only ~5% clear $100; median about $1.59. Dated snapshot with methodology: pokemondealfinder.com/market-data/pokemon-card-value-distribution.

Might be a useful data point if you update the guide.
